To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the results of two scenarios drawn up in 1989 for the Brazilian economy in the year 2010 show that the model structures have a strong influence on the findings.
the model structure affects the findings.
model structures affect findings and decisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do model structures affect findings and decisions?
the importance of the modelling approach in energy and CO  emission studies, particularly in the Brazilian case.
the question: how far can we trust the results of models?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of a model are dependent on the model's structure, but also on the data, the time horizon and the assumptions made by the modeller.
the model structures affect the results and the findings, but the impact of model structure on the results is not the only factor.
the model structure does not necessarily affect the findings of the model but it does affect the interpretation of the results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to obtain a reliable and consistent scenario, it is necessary to consider the economic and environmental impacts of alternative scenarios.
the results of the two models were not very different in terms of energy and CO  2 emissions.
, in the Brazilian case, the differences between scenarios are not as large as the uncertainties in the data and the assumptions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of model is not as important as the quality of the information used in the analysis.
the choice of a model is not the only factor to be considered in assessing the impacts of energy and environmental scenarios.
it is necessary to develop a new energy and CO ₂ emission scenario for Brazil that is more realistic and more consistent with the country’s energy policy.
